title: Cancer: current or history, and metastases
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cancer as documented at this visit.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for prostate cancer.

HPI: The patient is a 73-year-old male presenting for a follow-up visit regarding his diagnosis of prostate carcinoma. He is currently receiving radiation to manage the malignancy. He reports that he has been tolerating the treatment well thus far, noting some mild fatigue but no significant acute side effects. He denies any new-onset urinary symptoms or significant changes in his bowel habits. He expresses that his primary goal is to maintain his current quality of life while continuing his oncology regimen.

Medication List:
- Lysumi (radiation management)
- Advil (as needed for discomfort)
- Multivitamin

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Reports mild fatigue; denies fever, chills, or unintended weight loss.
Genitourinary: Denies dysuria or hematuria.
Musculoskeletal: Denies joint pain or significant mobility issues.
All other systems are reviewed and are negative.

Social History: The patient is retired and lives with his wife. He enjoys gardening and walking. He denies tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History: Father had hypertension. Mother had type 2 diabetes.

Vitals:
BP: 132/84 mmHg
HR: 72 bpm
Temp: 98.6 F
RR: 16 breaths/min
SpO2: 98% on room air

Recent Labs:
Hemoglobin: 13.2 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 7.4 x 10^9/L
Platelets: 210 x 10^9/L
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL
eGFR: 78 mL/min/1.73m2

Exam:
General: Well-appearing, alert and oriented x3.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, no masses palpable.
Genitourinary: No visible lesions or discharge.
Extremities: No edema noted.

Assessment:
1. Prostate cancer: The patient is on active treatment with radiation. Clinical status is stable.

Plan:
1. Continue current radiation schedule as directed by the oncology team.
2. Monitor for any increased fatigue or changes in urinary flow.
3. Follow up in four weeks for a reassessment of treatment tolerance.

Electronically signed,
H. Tanaka, NP
May 14, 2026
explanations: Cancer of the prostate under current treatment is a current malignancy: C61.

distractors.why: Treatment is still directed at the cancer, so it is current, not history.
